became the latest operator to enter public ownership on Sunday as Labour moved closer to renationalising all major passenger rail services,

reported. The commuter operator, which runs services between London Marylebone and Birmingham, was the sixth to be taken over by the state, with the remaining four expected to follow by the end of 2027. The Department for Transport said the move would improve reliability and ease overcrowding, promising more services and seats, new trains, upgraded stations and better onboard facilities including improved wifi.

. Speaking at an event in the US where Homan was present, the Reform UK leader urged Europe to take a "more sensible view" of the Trump administration rather than treating it as "villainous". Homan, a key adviser on US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, has faced scrutiny over the agency's aggressive enforcement tactics following several fatal shootings by ICE agents earlier this year.
